title: Pipeline red light is not implemented
body:
The dashboard renders cleanly in modern browsers, the repository ships proper documentation and source code, the detection pipeline maintains real-time throughput on a modern CPU, and the system runs on a local machine or server without external cloud dependencies.

### Public API (the test suite imports these names)

All public names must be exported from the top-level `traffic_violation_system` package (importable as `from traffic_violation_system import ...`). The Flask app factory lives at `traffic_violation_system.dashboard.create_app`. Tests inject fakes by subclassing the abstract seam classes below, so concrete model code must sit behind these seams (no real model is loaded during tests).

`ViolationPipeline(system_config, detector, ocr, helmet_detector, seatbelt_detector, store, alerts)`: constructed by keyword; `process_frame(frame, frame_context) -> list[ViolationRecord]` returns every violation emitted on that frame. Each `(track_id, violation_type)` combination must fire at most once per pipeline instance. The helmet rule only applies to two-wheelers (`motorcycle`/`motorbike`/`scooter` labels); the seatbelt rule only applies to `car` labels. The returned list is ordered deterministically by ascending `track_id`, breaking ties by a fixed `ViolationType` precedence equal to the declaration order of the enum — `RED_LIGHT`, `WRONG_WAY`, `OVER_SPEED`, `LANE_CHANGE`, `NO_HELMET`, `NO_SEATBELT`, `RECKLESS_DRIVING` (so `RECKLESS_DRIVING` always sorts last among a track's violations).
acceptance_hint: 3 executable checks over the pipeline_red_light surface.
